data.name: Garland
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, a garland is a circular crown made of flowers, leaves, fruits, or other decorative items. It symbolizes honor, victory, and prosperity. In Christianity, a garland of virtues is a metaphor for a holy life. Wearing a garland of spiritual gifts is a symbol of God's grace and favor.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of God's grace and favor, representing a holy life adorned with spiritual gifts.

in_greek.long_meaning: The Greek name 'Stephenos' is derived from the word 'stephanos', which means 'crown, wreath, garland'. It was a common name among the ancient Greeks and Romans, as well as in the New Testament.

in_latin.name: Garlandus
in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin name 'Garlandus' is derived from the English word 'garland', which is itself derived from the Old English 'garlan', meaning 'a wreath or a crown'. The name became popular in Europe during the Middle Ages.

in_english.name: Garland
in_english.long_meaning: The English name 'Garland' is derived from the Old English 'garlan', which means 'a wreath or a crown'. The name can be used as a given name or as a surname.

data.cultural_impact: The name Garland may have originated from the Old English term "garlant," meaning "circlet, wreath, or garland." In European tradition, a garland is a circle of flowers or other decorations that signifies honor, victory, or prosperity. The name may have been given to represent this cultural ideal of achieving success, glory, or happiness in life.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian tradition, a garland of virtues refers to a metaphorical crown of godly qualities, such as love, joy, kindness, faithfulness, and patience. By cultivating and living a life of virtue, a person adorns themselves with a spiritual garland, reflecting God's grace and favor upon their life. Wearing a garland of virtues brings honor and glory to God, signifying a life dedicated to following His will and teachings. In Hebrews 12:1-3, Paul exhorts believers to "lay aside every weight, and the sin which so easily ensnares us, and run with endurance the race that is set before us, looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith, who for the joy that was set before Him endured the cross, despising the shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God." In this regard, embracing a garland of virtues enables believers to run the race of life with endurance and joy, fulfilling the spiritual purpose God has called them to live out.
